findings.title: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?`, so it is never called
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers only consults `include_<attr>?` methods. `include_website_name` without `?` is dead code, so `website_name` is always serialized. Because `website_name` is not in `untrusted_attributes`, it is also exposed to anonymous viewers of TL0 users, even though `website` itself is hidden for them. This leaks the host of the website and defeats the restriction. The method should be `include_website_name?`, and it should also honour `scope.restrict_user_fields?`.

findings.title: Malformed URL handling and website without scheme
findings.body: `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` swallows all errors. For website values without a scheme, such as `example.com/foo`, `host` is nil, so website_name is nil. The old client-side `split('/')[2]` also returned nothing there, but the template now hides the website entirely because `model.website_name` is empty. `URI(...)` is also parsed three times. Parse once into a local variable. `path` may also be empty or contain a trailing slash, for example `http://example.com/` renders as `example.com/` when the hosts match.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain comparison treats unrelated domains as the same
findings.body: The branch comparing `website_host.split('.')[1..-1]` to `discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1]` only requires equal label counts and more than 2 labels. For multi-part TLDs, such as `a.co.uk` against `b.co.uk`, it compares `co.uk` with `co.uk` and wrongly shows the full path for an unrelated site. The branch is also only reachable when hosts have equal depth, so cases such as `www.example.com` against `a.b.example.com` are not handled consistently.

findings.title: Client-side website_name is not refreshed after saving preferences
findings.body: The template now reads `model.website_name`, which comes from the server. After the user edits `website` in preferences and saves, `website_name` on the model is not updated, since `save` only sends `website` and updates `bio_excerpt`. The profile therefore shows a stale or missing name until reload. The old computed property updated automatically.

findings.title: Missing test coverage for edge cases
findings.body: The new tests cover only three happy paths. Nothing covers an invalid or schemeless website, an empty website, the sibling-subdomain branch, or the TL0 anonymous case. The anonymous case would have exposed that `website_name` leaks for TL0 users, because `untrusted_attributes` in the spec does not include it.
